thread:
maria (sales_eng): Heads up — FinFlow POC kicks off Monday. Need a concise provisioning runthrough for: Hosted API key, Dedicated pool (2x A100), and VPC peering (customer VPC). Who owns what and minimal steps to get them live? cc @kevin (solutions) @anya (security)

kevin (solutions): Owners: sales_eng (maria) gets hosted keys + customer comms; infra (liu) handles dedicated pool + peering; security (anya) signs off on allowed config. Minimal steps: 1) Hosted key scoped to project, 2) infra form for dedicated GPU request, 3) VPC peering + route table + IP allowlist, 4) test generate -> validate latency and cost.

anya (security): Quick security checklist to attach to the runbook: data residency region, KMS/BYOK requirement, console SSO (SAML/OIDC) enablement, audit log retention (90d default), IP allowlist CIDRs, and whether customer will send PII. Also note we need their ARO/Network contact and an approved security questionnaire (we have template).

liu (infra): Infra bits (minimal):
- Dedicated pool request (form): include model, GPUs, expected sustained throughput, desired region, duration. Example YAML snippet we accept in the form:
```
model: gptj-13b-v1
pool_size: 2
gpu_type: a100-80gb
region: us-west-2
duration_weeks: 4
expected_qps: 5
priority: poc
```
- VPC peering: need customer account ID, target CIDR (no overlap), 2 subnets (private), and a list of outbound ports (443 to our egress). We'll create a peering connection and a one-way NAT in their VPC if they need egress.
- IP allowlist: provide their NAT/public IP(s) or CIDR block. For quick test we can accept a /32 and expand later.

liu (infra): Also, minimal SG rules: allow outbound 443, inbound TCP 22 only for our jumpbox (if requested). If they want Private deployment, that is a separate on-prem/VPC package and requires longer lead time (~2–3 weeks).

devops-bot: infra-request #234 created by liu: https://internal.redwood/infra/requests/234 — status: pending approval (auto-assign: infra-team) :robot_face:

jordan (acct_mgr): Customer asked about BYOK and audit logs — do we support customer-managed keys for the Dedicated pool? If not, we should propose Private eval. Also they want a cost estimate to include in their SOW.

anya (security): We support KMS integration for Private deployments and Dedicated can be BYOK if we onboard compliance paperwork (security review). I'll start the data flow diagram review once we have the questionnaire.

maria (sales_eng): I'll create the hosted API key today and scope to project tag "finflow-poc". What's the exact Console path?

liu (infra): Console -> Projects -> [finflow-poc] -> API Keys -> Create scoped key. Select scopes: "inference:generate" and "billing:view". For testing, set max_tokens_per_min to 60k.

kevin (solutions): Pricing note for SOW: 2x A100 reserved for 4 weeks + ingress/egress and storage for KV cache. Ballpark: $18k/week for pool reservation -> ~72k for 4 weeks before discounts. Add hosted usage estimate for dev testing (~$800). Will refine with exact model/seq length.

maria (sales_eng): I'll add cost placeholders and mark as "estimate". I'll also send the security questionnaire template to the customer and request network contacts and NAT/public IP.

anya (security): When you send the questionnaire, include this checklist line: "Is customer sending PII? If yes, CSAT and DPA required; provide approved contact."

kevin (solutions): Testing runbook (quick):
1) Create hosted key, run simple curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
2) Once dedicated pool is ready, update request header to use `X-Redwood-Pool: finflow-poc-pool` and run 50 concurrent calls from their test harness.
3) Validate tail latency under 200ms at target QPS. Failover: if pool not ready, route to hosted fallback model `gptj-13b-v1-fallback`.

liu (infra): I'll attach the peering template and the minimal routing policy to the infra request. Expect 1–2 business days for approval once the form has throughput justification.

maria (sales_eng): Great. Action items: 1) maria create hosted key + share to customer (today), 2) liu submit infra-request and share link (today), 3) anya send security questionnaire template (today), 4) kevin draft estimate and put into the POC doc (EOD). I'll follow up with customer network contacts.

kevin (solutions): I'll also add a short note in the doc about canary rollout & fallback policy so they know how we'll handle model regressions.

maria (sales_eng): Thanks all — I'll update this thread with the hosted key ID and infra request link once done. :thumbsup:
